description: We are a team of three young innovators participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Combining software development, scientific research, and UI/UX design, we aim to build an interactive application using NASA's NISAR satellite data to visualize changes on Earth's surface. Our mission is to turn complex satellite data into meaningful insights through creativity, teamwork, and technology.
summary: We designed a website where scientists and researchers can explore changes happening around the world using NASA's NISAR data. They can analyze satellite imagery, conduct research, observe changes over time, and compare different satellite images and datasets. We also added an API section to the platform. If our project is selected, we plan to further develop and improve it by adding more features and expanding its capabilities.
details:
NISAR Research Platform

Our project is a web-based research platform designed to make NISAR satellite data easier to explore and understand. It provides researchers and students with a simple way to search available NISAR products, view their geographic coverage on a map, examine metadata, and compare catalogue results.

The platform includes a Data Explorer, product filters, map visualization, temporal catalogue summaries, and HDF5 file structure inspection. Users can also export research results in CSV and PDF formats. The backend connects to the ASF data services to retrieve available NISAR catalogue information.

Our goal is to make satellite data more accessible and help people explore changes in different regions over time. This is an initial prototype, and we plan to improve its features, usability, and research capabilities in future versions.
